newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Bank of Mauritius doubled T-bills sales in January.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Mauritius doubled T-bills sales in January.

text.p: Treasury bills sold by the Bank of Mauritius almost doubled in January from December as the central bank continued its tight monetary policy, the Bank said in its monthly report for January issued on Friday.

"Over the five weekly auctions held in January 1997, the total amount of bills put on tender was 4.70 billion rupees showing an increase of 2.05 billion rupees over the preceding month," the central bank said.
"The value of bids received amounted to 5.62 billion rupees, out of which 4.68 billion rupees was accepted," it added.
During treasury bills auctions in December 1996, the central bank received bids totalling 2.48 billion rupees, out of which it accepted 2.37 billion rupees.

The report said the weighted yield of bills auctioned in January 1997 rose to 10.66 percent from 10.05 percent in December while the bank rate resulting from the weekly auctions, ranged between 10.41 and 10.72 percent in January from 10.01 to 10.34 percent in December.
"The market maintained its preference for 364 day bills during the month under review (January)," the report said.
"Commercial banks remained the major participants in the primary bill market with their market share increasing in January 1997 relative to the previous month," it added.
In the forex market, the Mauritian rupee strengthened against the currencies of its major trading partners in January except the dollar and South African rand, the bank said.
Forex dealers said central bank interventions in the forex market in January helped support the local currency against a strengthening dollar in international markets.
The bank sold $20.63 million and purchased $7 million during market interventions in January with the intervention ask rates ranging between 19.81 and 20.11 rupees for one dollar.

The rupee was quoted at the daily average of 20.112 against the dollar in January from an average 20.107 in December. Versus the pound, the rupee firmed to the daily average indicative rate of 33.431 in January from 33.451 in December.

In December, the central bank interventions sold $23.65 million to and purchased $18 million from the interbank forex market with the intervention ask rates ranging between 19.83 to 20.12 rupees to the dollar.
Sales of foreign currencies by the Mauritius Sugar Syndicate to banks totalled an equivalent of $4.32 million in January from $4.48 million in December, the report said.
It said forex reserves at the central bank amounted to 17.12 billion rupees at the end of January, representing 23.6 weeks of imports based on revised import bill value for fiscal 1995/96.
At the end of December, reserves at the central bank totalled 15.99 billion rupees, or 22.1 weeks of imports.
